summary: Nora's memory is taken off the open network, and her computer gets an alert when it is down, a backup, an audit trail for what happens to the machine, and a defined way out to PyPI and Ubuntu packages.
details: Honcho no longer needs to listen on every interface: nora reaches it by name on a private network, and a probe proves a container on the default bridge is refused. The steps that apply it on the host are in the runbook; merging does not apply them.
The computer's VM may fetch from PyPI and the Ubuntu archive and nothing else, set by the lifecycle script and read back from sbx's own policy.
A down or unreachable computer (including after a token rotation that did not reach Nora) raises an alert to the alert channel; with the computer off the series is absent, not down.
The VM's disk is backed up nightly to the host and verified; destroy takes a backup first and refuses without one unless told to.
VM create, recreate, restart, token rotation (by fingerprint) and policy-log reads are recorded as audit rows, spooled on the host and replayed into the database.
Token rotation is documented as two steps (restart the unit, recreate nora) with a check that the old token is refused and the new one accepted.
limitations: The Honcho port change, the egress rules, the backup timer and the config-only edit are host steps nobody has run yet: each is UNVERIFIED until read back on norty.
The backup is on the same host as the disk, so it is rollback and not off-host backup.
